papers.title_en: PULSE: Unlocking Practical Image Compression on Single-Thread CPU
papers.authors: Zhaoyang Jia, Tianyu Zhang, Zihan Zheng, Wenxuan Xie, Jiahao Li, Bin Li, Houqiang Li, Yan Lu
papers.evidence: 低复杂度学习式编解码，含整数线性CDF熵编码与元先验
papers.tldr: 学习图像压缩在CPU等资源受限硬件上计算开销高，难以实用。PULSE提出超低复杂度5.2 kMAC/像素神经接收器，并配合整数线性CDF预测器与元先验实现位精确熵编码。它还利用启发式探针驱动的智能体进化，通过人-LLM协作迭代改进架构。单线程CPU解码1080p仅126 ms，压缩性能接近HM，感知优化后可媲美MS-ILLM，推动CPU端实用部署。
papers.abstract_en: Despite recent progress in learned image compression, existing methods remain computationally expensive on resource-constrained hardware, particularly CPUs. We introduce PULSE, a practical codec that enables (1) low-latency decoding on diverse hardware platforms with an ultra-low-complexity 5.2 kMAC/pixel neural receiver, and (2) efficient bit-exact entropy coding with an integer linear CDF predictor and a meta prior. To recover compression performance under this tight budget, we introduce an agentic evolution process guided by heuristic probes that iteratively improves the architecture through human-LLM collaboration. PULSE decodes a 1080p image in 126 ms on a single CPU thread while achieving compression performance comparable to HM. After perceptual optimization, PULSE competes with larger perceptual codecs like MS-ILLM. Codes are at https://github.com/microsoft/GenCodec/tree/main/PULSE

papers.title_en: Krum-Inspired Central Teacher Selection and Residual Channel Bottlenecks for Efficient DeepSC
papers.authors: Rami Eid, Mostafa Jammoul, Omar Kaaki, Maria Slim, Mariette Awad, Hadi Sarieddeen
papers.evidence: 多教师知识蒸馏压缩语义通信模型
papers.tldr: 边缘设备部署 Transformer 语义通信模型需兼顾压缩与信道鲁棒性。本文研究多教师知识蒸馏压缩 DeepSC，提出残差信道瓶颈，把传输表示拆为基础流与残差流并做非等功率分配；同时用受 Krum 启发的中心性准则，从五模型集成中选单一中心教师，在 logit 与中间特征层蒸馏。EuroParl 上，两层学生在 AWGN 下恢复教师约 98% BLEU-1、93% BLEU-4、96% SBERT，Rayleigh 下约 89%、77%、87%，并减少 1.33 倍非嵌入参数、降低 1.79 倍单教师推理延迟；消融显示残差瓶颈贡献约 +8.4% BLEU-1，中心性选择较均值聚合提升约 +3.0%。
papers.abstract_en: Deploying transformer-based semantic communication models on edge devices requires compression that preserves semantic fidelity under channel variability. We study a compressed deep semantic communication (DeepSC) student trained by multi-teacher knowledge distillation and combine two ideas: (i) a residual channel bottleneck that splits the transmitted representation into a base stream and a residual stream with unequal power allocation, and (ii) a Krum-inspired, medoid-style centrality criterion that selects a single central teacher from a five-model ensemble, applied at the logit and intermediate-feature levels and combined with a feature-dominant distillation loss. On the EuroParl benchmark, a two-layer student recovers about 98% of the four-layer teacher's bilingual evaluation understudy (BLEU)-1 under additive white Gaussian noise, with 93% of its BLEU-4 and 96% of its sentence-BERT (SBERT) score, and about 89%, 77%, and 87% of the teacher's BLEU-1, BLEU-4, and SBERT, respectively, under Rayleigh fading, while reducing non-embedding parameters by 1.33x and single-teacher inference latency by 1.79x (9.0x relative to a five-teacher ensemble used here as an upper-bound reference, not a deployment baseline). Controlled ablations over three seeds indicate complementary contributions of about +8.4% BLEU-1 (+9.6% SBERT) from the residual bottleneck and +3.0% (+2.9% SBERT) from centrality-based selection over mean aggregation. A decoder-mode ablation shows that the base stream alone recovers about two-thirds of the full BLEU-1 while the residual stream alone collapses, supporting the role of the residual as a refinement on top of the base.

papers.title_en: WaterKron and FlipFlop Hessian: Information-Theoretically Grounded Quantization with Kronecker-factored Hessians
papers.evidence: 结合率失真与熵编码的量化
papers.tldr: 后训练量化通常依赖 Hessian 近似，但 Kronecker 分解 Hessian 应如何选择仍缺乏理论依据。WaterKron 将双边 GPTQ、行列相关 waterfilling 缩放和熵编码结合，并引入显式 Kronecker-Hessian 失配因子 Φ 推导高速率失真，量化近似带来的渐近失真惩罚。最小化 Φ 等价于高斯协方差拟合，可用经典 flip-flop 更新求解，从而为 FlipFlop Hessian 给出率失真论证与选择准则。实验表明，在多种设置下该 Hessian 在 KL 散度和困惑度上持续优于输入仅用、边缘及 Frobenius 基线，说明理论指导的 Hessian 选择能提升后训练量化。
papers.abstract_en: How should a Kronecker-factored Hessian approximation be chosen for post-training quantization? We address this question through WaterKron, which combines two-sided GPTQ with row- and column-dependent waterfilling scales and entropy coding. We derive its high-rate distortion with respect to the full Hessian using an explicit Kronecker-Hessian mismatch factor $Φ$. This factor quantifies the asymptotic distortion penalty due to the Kronecker Hessian approximation and provides a criterion for selecting the factors optimally. Minimizing $Φ$ leads to a Gaussian covariance-fitting problem with classical ``flip-flop'' updates. We thus give a rate-distortion justification for using the resulting FlipFlop Hessian in quantization. We evaluate it empirically, finding that the FlipFlop Hessian consistently improves KL divergence and perplexity over input-only, marginal, and Frobenius-based Hessian choices.
